task: W2-67 (DAEO-9nys) batch 1c test design — revise `test_w1_27_rebuild_r4.py::test_rebuild_codeintel_reason_is_measured` (red under plants, green on the head) and decide whether the rebuild mode's write-scope case should also snapshot the code-graph daemon's folder.
status: DONE — commit cb38b369 exists. The r4 case is revised: red under 4 plants, green on the head. In the r8 case only the comment changed: the daemon folder is written by design (DEC-338), so it is left out of the snapshot, with evidence.
work_completed: (1) Case `test_rebuild_codeintel_reason_is_measured` (name kept). It now runs three full rebuilds of tiny projects with this worktree's code. Each rebuild gets its own PATH: git and gitleaks, plus the code-index tool in one of three states the case sets itself. `answers`: a stand-in that answers every call with a successful MCP envelope; the case requires that the tool was asked `index_repository` and that the code index is `recreated`. `fails`: a stand-in whose tool calls exit 37; the case requires `not_recreated`, a reason naming `codebase-memory-mcp` and `37`, and no word of absence. `absent`: no tool on PATH; the case requires `not_recreated` and a reason naming the tool as not there. The old assertion (the reason is not "no code index module exists") is kept for all three, so no expectation is lowered. The case no longer uses the session copy of the whole tree. (2) Case `test_the_mode_writes_only_under_gov_runtime`: assertions unchanged; its comment now records why the daemon folder is not snapshotted. Every rebuild that reaches the code index creates `/tmp/gov-cbm-<uid>/<sha256(root)[:16]>/` for the tool's lock and socket files. It does so even when no tool is on PATH, and in the `--no-embeddings` mode too. DEC-338 puts those files there because a socket path is limited to 108 bytes, and says they are not index files. Snapshotting that folder would turn the case red on the head for something a decision allows. Snapshotting the whole `/tmp/gov-cbm-<uid>` would also catch other workers' concurrent rebuilds. (3) Added a batch 1c section to README-W2-67.md: the plant method, the fault table, red and green results, the daemon-folder evidence table, and the finding.
files_changed: tests/acceptance/W1-27/test_w1_27_rebuild_r4.py; tests/acceptance/W1-27/test_w1_27_rebuild_r8_no_embeddings.py (comment only); tests/acceptance/W1-27/README-W2-67.md. Written outside tests/acceptance/W1-27/, never committed: /home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-67/.gov-runtime/scratch/td-1c/{w2_67c_plant.py, w2_67c_child.py, r4-head.xml, r4-P67C-1.xml, r4-P67C-2.xml, r4-P67C-3.xml, r4-P67C-4.xml, r8-head.xml, final-head.xml}; pytest temp folders under /tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-67/td-1c. The daemon wrote its own folders under /tmp/gov-cbm-1000 during the runs; I never wrote there.
evidence: Commit cb38b369 "DAEO-9nys (W2-67): W1-27's code-index reason case reads the outcome and reason against a tool that answers, fails with exit code 37, or is absent; the rebuild mode's daemon folder is left out by design (DEC-338)", with trailers Task: DAEO-9nys / Role: independent-test-designer / Implements: DEC-889, DEC-898 / Rewrite-Reason: the assertion does not read what the case's name claims / Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. `git log --oneline -2` shows cb38b369 then 33b6aa5b; `git status --short` is empty. `gov.__file__` line: `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-67/src/gov/__init__.py`. Collection: `15774/15776 tests collected (2 deselected) in 12.28s`, no error. Plants for r4 (each run with `-p w2_67c_plant`, scratch folder on PYTHONPATH, src never written):
- P67C-1 (constant reason) → red: `the reason does not name the tool and the exit code 37 it answered with …: {'status': 'not_recreated', 'reason': 'codebase-memory-mcp did not answer'}`
- P67C-2 (outcome does not follow the measurement) → red: `the code index's tool answered, yet the code index is not recreated (DEC-440): {… "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'codebase-memory-mcp'"}`
- P67C-3 (round 4's fault: tool never asked, old constant reason) → red: `the code index reason is the constant 'no code index module exists' …`
- P67C-4 (exit code dropped from the reason) → red: `… 'reason': 'codebase-memory-mcp index_repository failed (exit code )'`

Head reasons: `answers` recreated; `fails` `codebase-memory-mcp index_repository failed (exit code 37)`; `absent` `[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'codebase-memory-mcp'`. Daemon folders seen: the r8 project → `/tmp/gov-cbm-1000/5647770e6d54062f/cbm-daemon-1000/` with 11 tool lock files; r4's answers/fails/absent projects → `a4dbfeebcbb4b9ae`, `36ad016e7173d362`, `43cba013bfc2633c` (empty, made even with no tool); under P67C-3 → no folder. Scratch figures: before 1 + 3 inodes, 4.0K + 12K; after 1,412 + 12 inodes, 23M + 48K (`/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-67/td-1c` + scratch/td-1c), far inside the 5 GB / 150,000 share. pytest kept three base folders (pytest-3, -4, -5); no `--basetemp` was passed.
tests: r4 case on the head: 1 passed in 8.81 s. r4 under P67C-1/2/3/4: 1 failed each (8.66 s, 8.62 s, 1.43 s, 8.59 s). r8 case on the head: 1 passed in 11.76 s. Final head run of both cases: 2 passed in 36.11 s (`final-head.xml`). Collect-only of `tests`: 15774/15776 collected, no error. All runs were foreground, one worker, never `-x`.
discoveries: (1) Nothing removes the code index's daemon folders. `/tmp/gov-cbm-1000` holds 11,014 of them, 138,273 inodes in all, one per project root any rebuild or code-index case ever used. Test project roots are new on every run, so every run adds folders, and `TMPDIR` does not move them. That is close to the size of one session's whole DEC-898 inode share (150,000). (2) The folder is created before the tool is asked, so even a rebuild with no tool on PATH leaves one. (3) `gov retrieve` gave no evidence: the worktree's lexical and semantic facets are `stale`, and refreshing them would write `.gov-runtime/` outside scratch.
risks: The `fails` stand-in lets the settings call succeed and fails only the `cli` tool call; that is how the head reports an exit code. A future implementation that fails at a different step and drops the exit code from its reason would turn the case red; I judge that correct under DEC-440's "measured reason". The stand-ins depend on the tool's external CLI shape (`cli … index_repository`, the MCP envelope), which is pinned at 0.11.0.
lessons: Outside the sandbox, a PATH of git, gitleaks and a shell stand-in makes the code index's outcome deterministic, with no real tool, in about 9 s for three rebuilds. To find a test project's daemon folder, take the first 16 hex digits of the sha256 of its resolved root under `/tmp/gov-cbm-<uid>`.
proposed_decisions: P-W2-67-TD1C-A: give the daemon folders a clean-up. Either `gov.codeintel` removes `daemon_dir(root)` when its session ends and no daemon holds it, or the suites' fixtures remove the folder of each temporary project they made, and W2-67's temp-folder KPI (DEC-898) counts `/tmp/gov-cbm-<uid>` among the places a run must not grow. Recommendation: both, the fixture side in W2-67's round 2 and the module side for W1-16's owner. Confidence medium. The owner decides.
unresolved: Read refusals met: 0. `gov retrieve` was used once, for DEC-440's rule; it returned no evidence (facets stale), so I read DEC-440, DEC-338, DEC-530, I4 §2.2's two rows, `src/gov/codeintel/__init__.py` and `src/gov/rebuild/command.py` (not this ticket's implementation). The code-graph tool had no project indexed, and indexing would have written its cache outside my paths, so I did not use it. The batch 1b "needs only git" package and the daemon-folder clean-up package remain open.
recommended_next_action: The ticket lead takes P-W2-67-TD1C-A into W2-67's temp-folder KPI (round 2) and passes the module-side clean-up to W1-16's owner.
